question: The appearance of a stick at the interface when immersed in water is an example of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __Refraction of light__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The phenomenon that causes a stick immersed in water to appear bent is known as refraction.
 
• Refraction occurs when light travels from one medium (such as air) into another medium (such as water) with a different optical density.
 
• **The change in density causes the light waves to change speed and directio**n.
 
• When light passes from air into water, it slows down and bends towards the normal (an imaginary line perpendicular to the water's surface).
 
• This change in direction is what causes the stick to appear bent when it is partially submerged in water.
 
• The light rays from the submerged portion of the stick undergo refraction at the air-water interface, creating the illusion of a bent stick.
 
• This** phenomenon is a result of the different refractive indices of air and water, which determine how light waves propagate through these mediums**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Reflection

 
 
• Reflection of Light may be defined as the bouncing back of the light ray by a smooth polished surface.
 
• We see objects around us due to this phenomenon of light.
 
• Reflection of light occurs through smooth polished surfaces like Plane mirror, Spherical mirrors (concave and convex).
 
• The bending of a light ray, when it passes from one medium to another is known as the Refraction of Light.
 
• It happens through lenses, prism, etc.
 
• Both Reflection and Refraction show the Particle Nature of Light.
 
 
 
• **Displacement**
 
 
• ​Light displacement (LDT) is the weight of a ship when it's fully equipped but not carrying any cargo, fuel, water, ballast, stores, passengers, or crew.
 
• However, the ship's boilers will contain water at the level needed for steaming. 
 
• Light displacement **is also known as "light weight"**.
 
• It's d**ifferent from loaded displacement, which is the weight of the ship plus its cargo, passengers, fuel, and stores**
 
 
 
• **Transmission**
 
 
• **​Light transmission** is the process of electromagnetic waves, like visible light, ultraviolet light, or radio waves, passing through a material.
 
• The amount of light that can pass through a material is measured as its transmission, which is usually expressed as a percentage. 
 
• **Light transmission can be either directional or diffuse, similar to reflection**
